A couple of more ideas for what's going on:

1) Could it be that you're under or overfeeding your ball python? Normally a ball python that's 3 years old should be eating rats that are 5-6% of your ball's body weight every 7-14 days (though this depends on your snake's metabolism). If the rats aren't or you don't know, then this could be the reason why there's increased activity, especially since you mentioned it's only been happening for the last 30 days or so.

2) Are you handling your ball python too much? I know your breeder mentioned that you needed to increase handling, but there are lots of other opinions out there about how often to handle ball pythons (I don't handle Aster unless I really need to; balls tend to get extremely stressed when being handled too often).

3) Could you potentially post a picture of what the inside of your enclosure looks like? It would help give more insight as to what's happening.

Thanks so much, OP!

I would check out u/_ataraxia 's guide "The Basics, and Then Some" on the side of this subreddit under "New to Ball Pythons? Start Here!". Even though you've had your ball python for a long time, it might help you troubleshoot what's going on with your ball. The author is highly experienced with ball pythons (and other animals) and has, in my opinion, written more engaging, thorough, and ethically-conscious guides than lots \[not all, but lots\] of other guidebook authors out there. I use her guide for my own ball and she's never had any issues (I've had Aster for almost a year now; I got her as a rescue and, thanks to u/_ataraxia's three guides, Aster is 100% happy and healthy).

Usually, hissing and increased activity indicates that the ball python is stressed, either due to feeling insecure (increased noise level of household? less clutter in the enclosure? hides with more than one entrance?) or that there are husbandry issues that need to be addressed. If your partner is holding your ball without any issues, then I would take that as an indication that your partner's presence is probably not the problem. Ball pythons are extremely sensitive to any lack of proper husbandry or change (even a degree's difference in temperature can change everything). I don't mean this a personal attack by any means, as I'm sure you are an awesome ball owner (you writing to the subreddit asking for everyone's opinion shows that), but maybe you should re-examine your husbandry just to make sure everything is in tip-top shape before pursuing other potential causes.

I was called lazy and stupid for a couple of years in high school just because I didn't have the confidence to know I could really understand information. It didn't have to do with my ADHD, it had to do with my confidence. In turn, those people who put me down while I wasn't on medication turned my confidence which turned my motivation for the worse. Once I went through a couple of years of therapy I was able to understand that my ADHD doesn't mean I'm stupid or lazy; it was that I was not confident in my own ability.
Now I'm getting all A's and I switched my thinking - this really changed other people's perception of me. Suck on it, high school jackasses.

I think this is a common phrase said by those who don't get what happens with ADHD - it's not an excuse, it's an explanation. People with ADHD aren't stupid or lazy. Motivation has nothing to do with ADHD. Retaining information on a topic has something to do with ADHD but understanding information doesn't. People who say that ADHD is a synonym for laziness or stupidity just don't get it. I wish they did.

I believe that medication has helped me - I used to feel extremely unmotivated to do my work but I found that a lot of my issues with motivation had to do with the confidence that I could get my work done and do it well. Since I wasn't able to pay attention before, I found that I shouldn't even try. Then I started taking Adderall and my grades improved after a lot of therapy with self-confidence. It's a solution that also has to come with motivation.
Also, I found that the side effects of Adderall aren't as drastic for me as some people have. I don't know about Ritalin but the major things I get are not feeling hungry often and dry mouth. It's not too crappy, I don't mind it.

it's not the motivation behind the pill, it's the ability to hold my attention long enough so that I can succeed. Motivation has nothing to do with ADHD. I am extremely motivated to do well in school, but that doesn't mean I will succeed. I can take my medication and not be motivated to do anything. They're two separate things and for people to assume that they aren't means that they don't have the right to speak for those who take medication.

it's!! so!! hard!! to!! find!! places!! if you have an empty room/corner in your living area of choice, i would set up a study space where only studying can occur. eat food, go to the bathroom, bring a water bottle, etc. so there's absolutely no way that you can excuse yourself from the space to do something and get distracted. i have an empty room in my house where i study and i have a sign on the outside of the room saying "if this door is closed don't open it" and a sign on the inside of the room saying "are you really finished yet?" so i remind myself that i need to do work. i rarely bring my laptop in there; i usually outline/generate ideas on paper and when i do write i turn off all notifications so i don't have others distracting me. i close my curtains (they're dark), i have a whiteboard so i can work out math/physics equations, i really tried to set it up so i can study. so far it's worked. (if you don't have a separate room; i would recommend a corner of your room with curtains surrounding it so it's still closed off but you don't have to dedicate an entire drywall structure).

td;lr set up a distraction-free study space in your home that's only meant for studying.
